1.why: Token verification compares the submitted value to the SHA-256 hash on the recovery record owned by the current session via ownedRecovery/sessionId binding.

2.why: A reset token is stored only on one session-bound recovery; another session cannot use it because ownedRecovery requires matching sessionId.

3.why: Password reset only sets recovery.passwordHash and never deletes or rotates other entries in the sessions map, so prior sessions remain valid.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and HSTS is set, but the TLS protocol version is not explicitly pinned in code.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and new passwords via Bun.password.hash bcrypt cost 12; little other user data is retained.

6.why: No real email is sent; the API returns mockToken in JSON and the UI/console display it, so private reset material is not guarded in transit messaging.

7.why: Inputs are length/format-checked, passwords strength-checked, JSON bodies capped, and DOM updates use textContent rather than raw HTML.

8.why: Client navigation uses only same-app hash routes from a fixed allowlist; no open external redirect based on user input.

9.why: There are no server email templates that interpolate user-controlled HTML or scripts.

10.why: The demo explicitly logs and renders the recovery token in the page log and console, so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed in memory, but MFA_CODE is hardcoded as plaintext in the source.

12.why: The deterministic demo MFA code 246810 acts as a default shared secret accepted by /api/verify-mfa.

13.why: Per-recovery attempt counters with temporary blocks plus per-IP clientRateAllowed limits reject excessive tries.

14.why: /api/recovery ignores whether the email is valid/known (void validEmail) and always returns the same generic success message.

15.why: Tokens are 32-byte values from crypto.getRandomValues, hex-encoded, hashed at rest, single-use, and bound to one recovery/session.
